to measured absolute or relative bioavailability and matched oral-versus-

L2 adds related experimental records for the same molecule and exact condition.

formulation, dose, study design, consistency, limitations, or why an L1 outcome

oral-bioavailability outcome.

records did not define the accepted gold outcome: never count them as extra gold
votes, and do not treat the L1/L2 name itself as a positive or negative label.

parent-condition context may apply to the query. It is not a positive-class
probability, an experimental result, or a substitute for reasoning about the
visible structure, endpoint, assay, species, formulation, exposure, and
condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

Use general medicinal-chemistry knowledge to interpret structures, but ground
every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: Verapamil, the closest structural analog, has absolute oral bioavailability of 22% (95% CI 17–29%) in fasted healthy volunteers (C24), a point estimate only marginally above the 20% threshold; norverapamil SR values are 49±14% fasted and 34±12% fed (C09, C21), but these are modified-release formulations and less transferable to the query.

Human liver microsomal and hepatocyte experiments consistently show verapamil has high intrinsic clearance (e.g., pooled HLM CLint 153–360 mL/min/kg and hepatocyte CLint 117–179 mL/min/kg, C90; scaled hepatic clearance 16.5 mL/min/kg, C84; HLM half-life 11.63 min with CLint 228 µL/min/mg, C92), indicating extensive hepatic first-pass loss for the verapamil scaffold.

evidence_gaps: No direct oral bioavailability measurement exists for the query molecule.
L6 hepatic clearance records are for verapamil, not the query; query-specific CLint is unknown.
The effect of the cyclic 1,3-dithiane 1,1,3,3-tetraoxide group on absorption and first-pass metabolism is unquantified.
Verapamil F CI (17–29%) straddles the 20% threshold, making analog transfer threshold-sensitive.
No query-specific permeability, solubility, or efflux data are available.
content.decision_summary: Predicted low (F<20%) because the closest direct analog verapamil has F only 22% (CI 17–29%) and L6 human liver data show high intrinsic/hepatic clearance for the verapamil scaffold (C84, C90, C92), while the query's cyclic bis-sulfone modification increases MW/TPSA and lowers logD/neutral fraction, making absorption less favorable; the combined mechanistic and physicochemical evidence supports F below the 20% threshold despite the absence of query-specific F data.
